newsitem.title: FRANCE: French air cargo agents advised to seek surcharge.
newsitem.headline: French air cargo agents advised to seek surcharge.

text.p: Several French air forwarding agents, told Reuters their professional association, SNAGFA, has informed them by letter to bill airlines' for fuel surcharges applied on freight before November 16.
Some airlines, notably Lufthansa, Air France and KLM, had implemented the surcharges from the beginning of the month, at the rate of 50 centimes a kilo.
The agents, who declined to be named, noted that SNAGFA members had previously voted unanimously to pay the surcharge, but only from November 16.

"On reflection, refusing to pay the surcharges before the date was not practicable, given that agents have obligations under the Cargo Account Settlement System (CASS). SNAGFA is now advising members to claim back fuel surcharges paid during the first fortnight in November and we are currently considering this option."

Another agent said: "We are now beginning to receive account statements for last month's business and they appear to show that a vast majority of airlines applied fuel surcharges from the beginning of November so as far as we are concerned we are likely to be making claims for reimbursement."

The agent added: It's hard to say at this point in time how much money this represents and will only have a clear idea at the end of December. We won't haggle if it only works out at peanuts, it's the principle that counts. The way in which the fuel surcharge was proposed - no consultation with agents and little or no prior notice on its implementation, still rankles with many agents." - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
